changes.old: (1) 첫 번째 제곱을 전개한다: $(t - 1)^2 = t^2 - 2t + 1$. (2) 두 번째 제곱을 전개한다: $(2t - 2)^2 = 4t^2 - 8t + 4$. (3) 두 번째 전개식 전체에 뺄셈을 분배해 모든 항의 부호를 바꾼다. (4) $t^2$ 항: 1 - 4 = -3, $t$ 항: -2 - (-8) = 6, 상수항: 1 - 4 = -3 이다. (5) 결과는 $-3t^2 + 6t - 3$ 이다. 따라서 정답은 $-3t^2 + 6t - 3$이다.

(1) Expand the first square. (2) Expand the second square. (3) Distribute the subtraction over every term of the second expansion. (4) Combine like terms. (5) Write the simplified result. So the answer is $-3t^2 + 6t - 3$.
changes.new: (1) Area of the poster: $(2t-2)^2 = 4t^2 - 8t + 4$. (2) Area of the photo: $(t-1)^2 = t^2 - 2t + 1$. (3) Uncovered area = poster minus photo: $4t^2 - 8t + 4 - (t^2 - 2t + 1)$. (4) Distribute the subtraction over every term and combine like terms: $3t^2 - 6t + 3$. So the answer is $3t^2 - 6t + 3$.

"to have examined"는 완료부정사로 requires의 목적어 자리에 시제상 불필요하고 어색하며, "one who examines"는 사람을 가리키는 명사구로 how절들을 목적어로 받을 수 없고, "an examination that considers"는 명사구 뒤에 관계절이 붙는 구조라 이어지는 how절들과 문법적으로 연결되지 않아 동사 뒤에 올바른 형태를 요구하는 규칙을 위반한다.

"Requires" takes a gerund as its object, and "examining" governs the three following how-clauses. "To have examined" (perfect infinitive), "one who examines" (a person, not an action), and "examine" (a bare verb) cannot serve as the object of "requires" here.

changes.old:
Text 1

The collapse of coral reefs following marine heatwaves is often described as a straightforward function of temperature: reefs that experience more degree-heating weeks bleach more severely and recover more slowly. Researchers who model reef futures under warming scenarios have generally relied on cumulative heat stress as the dominant predictor, arguing that once a thermal threshold is crossed, symbiotic algae are expelled regardless of other local conditions. This framework has been useful for generating broad regional forecasts, but it treats reefs largely as passive thermometers, responding uniformly to a single external variable while other site-specific factors are folded into statistical noise.

Text 2

Recent surveys of reefs that experienced nearly identical heat exposure during the same bleaching event found striking differences in mortality, differences that heat-stress metrics alone cannot explain. Reefs with strong wave action and higher nutrient flushing retained more of their coral cover than sheltered reefs with comparable degree-heating weeks, suggesting that local water circulation modulates how corals experience thermal stress. Some researchers now argue that regional forecasts built solely on cumulative heat exposure will systematically misestimate which specific reefs survive, since circulation patterns can either compound or partially offset the physiological damage caused by elevated temperature.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that "once a thermal threshold is crossed, symbiotic algae are expelled regardless of other local conditions"?
